official.description: The Graduate Scholarship for Excellent Foreign Students (GSFS) supports non-Korean applicants currently enrolled or graduated from eligible countries who apply and are accepted into SNU and who apply for a designated college or school participating in the GSFS Program. applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship is decided by whichever SNU college or school you apply to, not by a central committee, which means your admission documents are doing double duty as your scholarship application and there is nothing extra to submit. The two hard gates are both institutional: you must be a non-Korean applicant enrolled or graduated from one of SNU's currently listed eligible countries, and you must be applying to a college or school that is actually participating in the GSFS for that semester. Both lists change every semester, so a scheme that was open to your country and your department last intake may not be this one - check the guide SNU's Office of Global Affairs circulates each semester rather than relying on last year's information. The money is full tuition exemption for up to four semesters plus a minimum of 500,000 KRW a month for living costs, with the exact amount varying by major, but there is no published airfare or insurance component so you will need to fund your own travel. Roughly 20 people get it each semester, and if you are also selected for the SNU President Fellowship Program you must pick one and give up the other.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean applicants from SNU's currently listed eligible countries applying to a participating SNU graduate college or school, with strong admission documents.
application_readiness_checklist: Get the current semester's GSFS guide from the SNU Office of Global Affairs and confirm both your country and your target college/school are on the lists
Check the 'Application for Scholarship' box during the online admission application to SNU's Office of Admissions - miss this and you are not considered at all
Prepare the admission documents for your target college or school to selection standard, since those documents are the entire basis of the scholarship decision
Confirm the admission application period for the semester you want to enter and treat it as your scholarship deadline
Decide in advance how you would choose between GSFS and the SNU President Fellowship Program if both were offered
Budget for airfare, insurance and settlement yourself, since no travel or insurance component is published for GSFS
common_rejection_risks: Failing to tick the 'Application for Scholarship' box in the online admission application, which silently removes you from consideration
Applying to a college or school that is not participating in the GSFS Program for that semester
Being from a country that is not on the current eligible-country list, which changes every semester
Assuming last semester's eligible-country or participating-college list still applies
Submitting weak admission documents, since the college or school selects purely on those
Expecting airfare or insurance to be covered, which GSFS does not state
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to and from Korea, health insurance, settlement and arrival costs, and any shortfall between the minimum 500,000 KRW monthly living expense and your actual costs. SNU's Office of Global Affairs publishes separate budget guidance for international students.
document_audit: There is no separate scholarship document set - the admission documents submitted to your college or school are the scholarship evidence, so they must be complete and selection-grade
The 'Application for Scholarship' checkbox in the online admission application is the single mechanism for entering the running, so confirm it before submitting
The eligible-country and participating-college lists live in the per-semester guide from the Office of Global Affairs, not permanently on the website
If you are selected for both GSFS and the SNU President Fellowship Program you must choose one, so understand both offers before deciding
alerts: The eligible-country and participating-college lists change every semester, so verify them fresh for your intended intake
SNU marks this page as last updated in 2023, so figures should be reconfirmed against the current semester's guide
Approximately 20 recipients per semester means the pool is small relative to applicant numbers
GSFS and the SNU President Fellowship Program are mutually exclusive if you are selected for both
The living expense is a minimum of 500,000 KRW per month and varies by major, so do not budget on the minimum if your field pays more
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission to a participating SNU graduate college or school through the SNU Office of Admissions online application during the international student admission period, tick the 'Application for Scholarship' box, and let the college or school select on your admission documents.
